relations.evidence: They stayed for another two years in the local Drakkar Monastery (Zhaqie/jia [札/扎伽/迦], Tib. Brag dkar dgon), where they studied under the elder Dpal ldan bstan 'dzin snyan grags (1866-1928, Drakkar Lama)

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: and in 1931 reached Chamdo (Changdu [昌都], Tib. Chab mdo) to study under Amdo Geshe, from whom he received about 40 tantric initiations and many teachings.

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: He was admitted at the Drepung Monastery (Tib. 'Bras spungs dgon pa), where he resided for two years.

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.object: Pha bong kha pa dbe chen snying po
relations.evidence: He also received teachings and initiations from the famous Pha bong kha pa dbe chen snying po (1878-1941).

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: In 1934, Taixu asked Fazun to return to China to direct the newly founded Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute in the Jinyun Monastery (縉雲寺) near Chongqing.

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: He then spent a few more months in Lhasa, where he was able to study under the Dharma Master Byang rtse chos rje (Jiangze fawang [絳則法王]; d.u.) at Ganden Monastery.

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: he was summoned to Beijing and was employed as a translator for the Committee for Minority Affairs

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: in 1956 he was nominated vice president of the Chinese Institute for Buddhist Studies (Zhongguo Foxue yuan [中國佛學院]).

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: He was then chosen to be the president of the Chinese Institute for Buddhist Studies, which had just reopened, a position he kept until his death.

relations.subject: Fazun
relations.evidence: With Dayong's death, Fazun inherited his role in Taixu's plans.
